note: R10 (zero non-Rust official gates). Every official BANZA engine AND every official gate is now Rust. The repository-hygiene gates (purity, operator contamination, invariant registry, OpenAPI compatibility) are the Rust crate engines/banza-repo-guards; their shell scripts in tools/ are thin RUST_WRAPPER_ONLY wrappers and need no entry here. The R2 website evidence adapter (website/components/home/banzaiKb.ts) is RUST_WRAPPER_ONLY over engines/banzai-evidence. Test files that exercise engines (e.g. services/banzai-api/test/pipeline.test.js) are classified TestAllowed by the guard — tests are permitted by the Rust-first rule and need no entry. Non-marker orchestration/smoke scripts (infra validators, assert-reference-svgs) carry no engine markers and are classified NotEngine without an entry. Cross-repo (banzai) legacy is tracked in the banzai repo's own allowlist, not here. THE BANZA ALLOWLIST IS NOW EMPTY: zero P0/P1 active legacy, zero pending migration, zero blockers. Paths ending in /** are directory globs.

entries.reason: wasm-bindgen glue GENERATED from the Rust decision engines (banza-operator-manifest / -conformance / -trust / -l2-readiness / -l3-readiness / -evidence-bundle) for the ADR-034 endpoint-originated validation journey. The engine is Rust; these .js files are compiled output vendored for nodejs, exactly like src/rustkb/. No hand-written decision logic; not a new non-Rust engine.

ADR-034 endpoint-originated journey orchestrator: resolves the target via the Rust registry (banza-target-registry WASM), fetches artifacts via the Rust fetcher (banza-artifact-fetcher), runs the Rust/WASM engines on fetched content and assembles OperationReceipts. Rust decides every verdict; this file only sequences the Rust calls and shapes receipts. Carries the 'evidence_bundle' token only as a journey-step / receipt-field label, not as an engine implementation.

BZC-4 cross-protocol RESOLUTION coverage harness — drives the Rust entity+artifact+scope resolver (artifact::resolve_scope, via knowledge.js → committed WASM) over a combinatorial matrix and asserts the four zero-tolerance criteria. It is an EVAL/TEST harness (imported by services/banzai-api/test/bzc4-coverage.test.js and run by tools/check-banzai-bzc-coverage.sh), not a runtime engine: it DECIDES nothing, calls no model, touches no network. It trips the strong-marker scan solely on artifact_type LABELS ('evidence_bundle'/'signed_metadata'/'revocation'/'conformance') used as expected-value strings in the coverage matrix — the same label-only basis as the allowlisted eval/e2e harnesses. Not a new non-Rust engine.

Canonical-eval SEED module (Increment 7, §19) — human-authored semantic seeds + programmatic case generators (surface/paraphrase variations, entity×artifact and metric×aggregation matrices, multi-turn, negative and zero-tolerance adversarial cases). It is pure DATA + string templating for an EVAL/TEST dataset: it DECIDES nothing, calls no model, touches no network, and re-implements NO engine logic — every generated expectation is validated against the committed Rust engine by eval/canonical-checks.mjs (RUST_WRAPPER_ONLY over knowledge.js → WASM) and dropped if unconfirmed. It trips the strong-marker scan solely on the artifact_type LABEL 'evidence_bundle' used as an expected-value string in the artifact matrix — the exact label-only basis on which eval/bzc-coverage.mjs is allowlisted. Not a new non-Rust engine.

BZC-2 live-artifact tool — the read companion of the allowlisted src/validate.js. Given the Rust-decided entity+artifact+scope (engines/banzai-query-core artifact::resolve_scope), it resolves the target in the Rust registry (banza-target-registry WASM) and obtains ONE implementation artifact via the Rust fetcher (banza-artifact-fetcher), then shapes a typed observation + OperationReceipt-style provenance for display. Rust decides entity/artifact/scope, the Rust registry resolves the target + endpoints, and the Rust fetcher enforces ALL egress authority (HTTPS-only, host pin, private/loopback/metadata blocklist, no redirects, size/time caps, TLS + media-type checks). This file DECIDES no verdict, accepts NO caller URL, and generates no evidence bundle; it only sequences the Rust calls and renders the result. It trips the strong-marker scan solely on the domain LABELS 'evidence_bundle'/'signed_metadata'/'revocation'/'conformance' used as artifact_type→endpoint keys — the same label-only basis on which validate.js is allowlisted. banzai-api service/glue (ADR-036), not a new non-Rust engine.

Durable validation-receipt store — the persistence companion of the allowlisted src/validate.js. It PERSISTS what the Rust engines already decided (append-only Postgres store + service-local outbox retry) and verifies receipt integrity via canonical-JSON SHA-256; it DECIDES no verdict, generates no evidence bundle (the Rust banza-evidence-bundle engine does that, via validate.js — this only INSERTs the produced bundle), and runs no protocol/financial logic. This is banzai-api service/glue (ADR-036: banzai-api is TypeScript service/glue over the Rust engines), not an official engine. It trips the strong-marker scan solely on the domain LABELS 'evidence_bundle' (the receipt-store table/column name) and 'canonicalJson' (a standard canonical-JSON serializer used for the integrity hash) — the same label-only basis on which validate.js is allowlisted. No hand-written decision logic; not a new non-Rust engine.

Durable-receipt E2E harness (receipts-e2e.mjs + receipts-down-child.mjs) — a TEST that drives the real receipt store + fail-safe facade + outbox against an ephemeral Postgres (run by run-receipts-e2e.sh / make receipts-e2e). Kept OUTSIDE services/banzai-api/test/ so `node --test` (npm test) does not auto-run these DB/Docker-dependent scripts as unit tests; hence a dedicated e2e/ dir + explicit allowlist entry. They exercise the engines' persistence companion; they DECIDE no verdict and are not a runtime engine. They trip the strong-marker scan only on the same domain LABELS (canonicalJson/evidence_bundle) as the allowlisted src/receipts/**.

Browser-side client for the durable validation-receipt routes (GET /validate/executions|execution|compare, POST /validate/reproduce|cancel). Pure fetch/shape glue for the Next.js UI — no protocol/financial/decision logic; the Rust engines decide and the banzai-api server persists. It trips the strong-marker scan only on the receipt-domain LABELS (evidence_bundle / reproduction_result / OperationReceipt) it must name to type the responses, exactly like the website/lib/*.ts WASM adapters. Not a new non-Rust engine.

Browser-side SSE client for the SPR-2 progressive endpoint (POST /banzai/ask/stream). Pure fetch + ReadableStream transport glue for the Next.js chat UI: it parses the typed Channel-A progress events and, on the terminal event, maps the EXACT same /ask envelope the non-stream route returns via mapAskResponse (the ONE shared mapper in the allowlisted UI surface website/components/home/banzaiKb.ts). It DECIDES no verdict, runs no protocol/financial/conformance/trust logic, calls no model, and re-implements NO engine — the Rust backend decides and progressContract.js owns the contract. It trips the strong-marker scan only on the domain LABEL 'banzaikb' (it imports mapAskResponse/buildAskBody from banzaiKb.ts) — the same label-only basis on which website/components/banzai/suggestions.ts and website/lib/banzaiValidateClient.ts are allowlisted. banzai-api/website UI glue (ADR-036), not a new non-Rust engine. SAFETY: no model prose ever reaches the UI before the terminal FINAL_VALIDATED/HONEST_FALLBACK envelope; a REFUSED disposition / refused boundary is surfaced as a refusal; any stream failure falls back to the non-stream fetch.

BanzAI answer-chip PRESENTATION helper — from an answer's already-decided shape (the /ask envelope: the Rust-decided intent, resolved entity, scope, which tools ran, the typed terminal/fallback kind) it selects which 0-4 follow-up CHIP STRINGS the Next.js chat UI offers. It DECIDES no verdict, runs no protocol/financial/conformance/trust logic, calls no model, touches no network, and re-implements NO engine — it maps envelope fields to Portuguese UI copy, exactly the presentation role the M2.9A suggestions (inside the allowlisted UI surface website/components/home/banzaiKb.ts) played before. It trips the strong-marker scan only on the domain LABELS it must name — 'evidence_bundle' (a suggestion string / operational-intent key) and 'banzaikb' (the KbKind type import) — the same label-only basis on which website/lib/banzaiValidateClient.ts is allowlisted. banzai-api/website UI glue (ADR-036), not a new non-Rust engine. SAFETY: a boundary/refusal answer receives only fixed safe reframes that never point at the refused action.

Build-time WHITEPAPER FIGURE GENERATOR — draws the 24 monochrome SVG figures (12 sections x PT/EN) for the docs/whitepaper LaTeX/web editions from the single content source. Not a runtime engine: no protocol/financial/decision logic, no runtime path, produces static SVG art only (like its sibling tools/whitepaper-latex.py, which carries no marker). It trips the strong-marker scan solely because it embeds the legitimate English figure LABELS 'fail-closed' (security diagram, fig9) and 'disabled (fail-closed)' (state diagram, fig12), which are the correct EN terms rendered in the English whitepaper figures — not engine markers.

Build-time PROJECTION of the lexical routing index: reads services/banzai-api/src/knowledge.js and writes engines/banzai-query-core/src/entries-index.json, emitting the entries whose canonical source declares lexicalCandidate: true, in registry order. It DECIDES nothing — membership is declared in the canonical source and the generator only copies the declared subset, refusing to write an empty, duplicated or keyword-less result. The scoring, coverage and routing that consume the index are Rust (banzai-query-core). It trips the strong-marker scan solely because a comment NAMES the Rust consumer of the artifact it writes, which is documentation of the boundary rather than a crossing of it.
